# Jobs Overview

## Overview

Every order in OrderHub is made up of one or more **jobs**. A job represents a single line item that needs to be produced — for example, one canvas print or one set of photo prints. Jobs have their own status lifecycle that is closely tied to the parent order's status and drives automation across the Production Board and OrderHub Downloader.

---

## Job Statuses

Jobs move through the following statuses during their lifecycle:

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **New** | The job has been created and is waiting to be picked up for production. This is the default status for all new jobs. |
| **In Production** | Work has started on this job. This can be set manually, via the Production Board, or automatically by OrderHub Downloader. |
| **Completed** | The job is finished and ready for the customer. |

### Custom Statuses

Organisations can define up to **two custom status labels** (e.g. "On Hold", "Awaiting Artwork") under **Settings → Processes**. Custom statuses act as sub-states of **New** — the job is still in the "New" phase of the workflow, but the label provides more detail about where it sits.

- Custom statuses appear as additional columns on the Production Board between **New** and **In Production**.
- Dragging a job into a custom status column updates its label while keeping the underlying status as New.
- Moving a job to **In Production** or **Completed** clears the custom status label automatically.
- Custom statuses follow the sequence defined in your configuration, so the Production Board columns always appear in the correct order.

---

## How Job Statuses Affect Order Status

Job and order statuses are linked by automated rules. You do not need to manually update the order status in most cases — it responds to job changes automatically.

### When a job moves to In Production

If the parent order is in **Pending** or **Confirmed** status, it is automatically moved to **In Production**. This signals that work has begun on at least one item in the order.

### When a job is marked as Completed

The system counts how many jobs on the order are completed:

- **All jobs completed** — The order is automatically moved to **Ready**, indicating the entire order is finished and can be collected or shipped.
- **Some jobs completed, but not all** — The order remains in (or moves to) **In Production**, reflecting that work is still ongoing.

### When an order is manually set to Ready, Shipped, or Completed

If an operator manually moves an order to **Ready**, **Shipped**, or **Completed**, all associated jobs are automatically marked as **Completed**. This is a convenience shortcut — if the order is done, all its jobs must be done too.

---

## Jobs on the Production Board

The Production Board is the primary interface for managing job status during production. See the [Production Board](./production-board) article for full details.

### Status View

The **Status View** displays a column for each status: **New**, any custom statuses, **In Production**, and **Completed**. Drag a job card between columns to change its status. The order status updates automatically based on the rules above.

### Timeline View

The **Timeline View** groups jobs by due date rather than status. Dragging a card between columns changes the job's **due date**, not its status. Use this view for scheduling and prioritisation.

### Visual indicators on job cards

| Indicator | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| Red border | The job is **overdue** — the due date has passed. |
| Amber border | The job is **due today**. |
| Speech bubble icon | The job has a **customer note** attached. Hover to preview. |
| Pencil icon | The job has **production notes**. Hover to preview. |
| Process badge | The job is linked to a production process (e.g. "Digital Print", "Framing"). |
| Outsourced badge | The job has been sent to an external supplier. Shows current supplier status. |

---

## Jobs and OrderHub Downloader

OrderHub Downloader (OHD) is the desktop application that pulls jobs and their artwork files to local production machines. Job status plays a key role in how OHD interacts with the queue.

### Pending jobs queue

OHD polls for jobs that are in **New** status and have not yet been received. A job appears in the OHD queue when:

1. Its status is **New** (including custom sub-statuses).
2. It has **not been marked as received** (`ohd_received_at` is empty).
3. It has **artwork uploaded** — either via manual upload or from a Pixfizz website (Pixfizz orders are included even without uploaded artwork, as artwork is delivered separately via manifest).
4. Its linked process does **not** have the "Disable Sending to OHD" flag enabled.

### OHD status progression

OHD drives job status through three stages:

| OHD Action | Job Update |
|------------|------------|
| **Received** | OHD marks the job as received, recording the machine name and download path in `ohd_received_details`. The job disappears from the pending queue for all OHD instances. |
| **In Production** | OHD marks the job as **In Production**. The job must have been received first. This also triggers the order to move to In Production if applicable. |
| **Completed** | OHD marks the job as **Completed**. If all jobs on the order are now complete, the order automatically moves to **Ready**. |

### Multi-instance behaviour

If multiple OHD instances are running (e.g. at different workstations), the first instance to poll a job claims it. Once marked as received, the job is invisible to all other instances. This is a first-come, first-served model.

### Location filtering

OHD instances are assigned to a store location. Jobs are filtered so that each instance only sees jobs relevant to its location. Processes with **location overrides** route jobs to specific sites regardless of the order's pickup location.

---

## Updating Job Status via API

Job status can also be updated programmatically via the OrderHub API. This is useful for integrating external production systems.

### Endpoint

`POST /functions/v1/update-job-status`

### Authentication

Include your API key in the `X-API-Key` header.

### Request body

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `job_id` | Yes | The UUID of the job to update. |
| `status` | Yes | The new status: `New`, `in_production`, `completed`, or a valid custom status. |
| `production_notes` | No | Optional notes (max 5,000 characters) to attach to the job. |

### Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "job_id": "uuid",
  "old_status": "New",
  "new_status": "in_production",
  "updated_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
}
